Moe Gangat on OTF Vonnie Taking the Stand in Lil Durk’s Trial
Lul Tim on Getting Call Lul Pab Killed in LA, Quando Leaving Rollin 60s Crips After That (Flashback)
recentItems.description: In this flashback, Lul Tim discussed the tragic events surrounding the death of Lul Pab, who was with Quando Rondo when assailants opened fire at a gas station near the Beverly Center. Lul Tim recalled the sorrow he felt after receiving the news while under house arrest, expressing disbelief and anguish over the loss. In his interview with DJ Vlad, Quando Rondo reflected on holding Lul Pab as he died and expressed regret over his ties to the Rollin' 60s Crips, eventually renouncing his affiliation. Lul Tim also shared insight into Quando's decision to step away, acknowledging the challenges he faced and realizing that some of those associated with the group were not supportive.

recentItems.title: Chingy & Vlad Agree: Industry People Like NORE are Fake & Full of Empty Promises (Part 1)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
---------
Chingy returns to VladTV for a candid conversation with DJ Vlad about trust, loyalty, and broken promises in hip-hop media. The St. Louis rapper opens up about years of attempted bookings with NORE and the frustration of watching others get opportunities while he was repeatedly given the runaround. Vlad connects the issue to his own public dispute over podcast appearances, comparing today’s interviews to major album features and arguing that creators may need contracts when platforms like Drink Champs and VladTV exchange guests.

The discussion also touches on social media accountability, “fake industry” relationships, and why Chingy says authenticity still matters. Later, Vlad asks about the Keefe D legal situation tied to the Tupac Shakur murder case, leading Chingy to share his views on Tupac, Biggie Smalls, walkie-talkie claims, security, and police involvement theories.

recentItems.title: Were You Surprised OTF Jam Testified Against Lil Durk?? 😳
Moe Gangat: Prosecutors Used Durk’s Lyrics, Videos & Podcast Clips Against Him (Part 2)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 1: https://youtu.be/fjE20W3ouPQ
--------
Attorney Moe Gangat joins VladTV to break down the latest testimony in the federal case involving Lil Durk, explaining why he believes the prosecution’s presentation has created serious challenges for the defense. Gangat analyzes the impact of cooperator testimony from “Vonnie,” contrasting it with earlier statements from OTF Jam, Flacka, Keith Jones, and Hester, and details how alleged proximity to Durk before the Los Angeles shooting became a key issue in court.

The discussion also examines how prosecutors played rap lyrics, music videos, and podcast clips to frame Durk’s public image and alleged role, raising broader questions about “murder music,” hip-hop evidence, and lyrics being used in criminal trials. Gangat also explores possible defense strategies, including challenging Vonnie’s credibility, his ties to King Von, claims about money, travel, Sherman Oaks, Miami, Georgia, and life after leaving Durk’s circle.

Charleston White joins DJ Vlad to break down the latest dispute between Boosie Badazz and Rod Wave after Rod reportedly sampled older Boosie records controlled by Trill Entertainment, then offered Boosie $100,000 as a gesture of respect. White argues Boosie should have accepted the money, comparing it to his own experience with Lil Uzi Vert and Capitol Records after being sampled in a TV interview.

Vlad also revisits his business fallout with Boosie, including interview fees, VladTV revenue, Patreon, Ricky Smiley, DJ Akademiks, Sean Cotton, and Big Loon’s comments about platform payouts. The conversation expands into music catalog ownership, sampling rights, independent catalogs, artist leverage, and how public narratives around Boosie have shifted amid controversies like the alleged Trump pardon situation.

--------
Hit-Boy opens up to Elliott Wilson and Vlad about resilience in the music business, his complicated history with Kanye West, and the pain of realizing their mentor-protégé relationship would never be the same. The Grammy-winning producer reflects on Kanye’s harsh comments about the late Virgil Abloh, explaining why he now tries not to take Ye’s outbursts personally. The conversation also touches on Kanye’s mental health, medication, controversial public statements, and Vlad’s scrapped interview plans around the Bully album. From early Kanye sessions at Record Plant in LA and Common’s Be era to The College Dropout, “Through the Wire,” and “Stand Up” for Ludacris, the interview revisits Ye’s producer-to-rapper evolution. Hit-Boy also discusses being boxed in creatively, following his passion as an artist, and teaming with The Alchemist for Goldfish after seeing producer-rappers thrive on stages like Rolling Loud.

recentItems.title: Judge Mathis on Why Lil Durk Shouldn't Take the Stand (Part 4)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 3: https://youtu.be/nviTlE7b-aE
Part 1: https://youtu.be/lOCPGaKuQxw
--------
Judge Mathis joins Vlad for a legal breakdown of the Lil Durk case, focusing on the prosecution’s burden to prove intent beyond a reasonable doubt. The discussion examines the aftermath of King Von’s death, Quando Rondo, Lul Pab, alleged motive among Von’s close associates, and how a cooperating witness’s contradictions could affect the jury.

Mathis explains why Durk’s defense may argue that any alleged plan was not murder, but something less severe, and why motive could point to others closer to King Von. He also addresses claims about Durk’s attempted flight, private flight tickets, and whether that could be framed as “consciousness of guilt.”

Most importantly, Judge Mathis says Durk should not testify, warning that defendants risk being tripped up by trained prosecutors during cross-examination.
